observed_contract: server prepares one governor admission for the initially preferred account
qwen-client may fail over inside the same logical operation from account A to account B
no sibling-account requestGovernor.before(B) is performed by qwen-client
quota telemetry is rebound to the final response account and emits one governor outcome at response finish
risk: sibling failover traffic can bypass per-account admission, token reservation, burst pressure and penalty waits
the initial account can retain a stale in-flight reservation after its failure
the governor can miss the pressure class that caused the failover because the final response account overwrites telemetry ownership
candidate_contract: every account that can reach provider I/O in one logical operation must have its own governor admission before that account's first provider call
every failed account attempt must settle exactly its own admission before failover continues
the successful final account keeps its admission until final usage is known, then success(account, usage) settles it
no account may receive success/failure for a reservation owned by another account
the existing bounded failover budget remains unchanged
limits: no hosted CI, Windows, Cloudflare, secrets or real accounts
